query: An equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy has a simple solid-solution structure and favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength, while its microstructure and deformation behavior remain insufficiently understood. Under hardness testing and mechanical loading of this starting state, what single intervention could overcome the strength and hardness limitation while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics? State the proposed intervention, its mechanism, the predicted measurable change relative to the unmodified alloy, its applicable processing and test conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a microstructural and mechanical experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of niobium (Nb) to the CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy will improve its strength and hardness while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with a simple solid-solution structure
generation.intervention: Addition of niobium (Nb) to the alloy
generation.conditions: High-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of Laves phase (Co2Nb-type, HCP) and lattice distortion in the FCC matrix
generation.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening due to the formation of hard, brittle Nb-rich Laves phase
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and hardness, with a potential optimal balance at a certain Nb content (e.g., 5 wt%)
generation.baseline: CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy without Nb addition
generation.boundary: Nb content range (0-9 wt%) and processing conditions (high-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering)
generation.uncertainty: Optimal Nb content and processing conditions for achieving the best balance of strength, hardness, and mechanical characteristics

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and Vickers hardness testing of CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloys with varying Nb contents (0-9 wt%)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Nb does not improve the strength and hardness of the alloy, or if the optimal balance is not achieved at a certain Nb content, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does doping with different Nb contents (0–9 wt%) affect the microstructure, mechanical properties, and fracture behavior of CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys prepared by high-energy ball milling and discharge plasma sintering?. System: CoCrFeNi-Nbx (x = 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 wt%) high-entropy alloys. Processing: High-energy ball milling (400 rpm, 4 h total with 10 min cooling intervals) followed by discharge plasma sintering (SPS) at 1100 °C, 30 MPa pressure, for 10 min; heating rates: 100 °C/min (0–600 °C), 50 °C/min (600–900 °C), 25 °C/min (900–1100 °C). Test conditions: Room temperature tensile testing (cross-sectional area 1.5 mm × 1 mm, tensile rate 0.2 mm/min, original gauge length 5 mm); Vickers hardness (500 g load, 15 s retention); XRD (Cu Kα, 40 kV, 40 mA, 20–90°); SEM/EDS analysis.
